item.title: Comfort Workshop
item.description:
The brief

Comfort Workshop makes British-made riser recliner chairs around the person who will use them. Unlike a standard online purchase, every order carries a considered set of choices — from the consultation and quote to the final specification the workshop uses to build the chair.

The brief was to create more than a brochure website: a connected digital platform for the entire journey. It should help customers find the right product, help the team capture and carry the detail of each order, and give production, delivery and aftercare a clear route from an agreed specification to a finished chair in the living room.

item.title: Rennix Automotive
item.description:
The brief

Rennix Automotive wanted a super quick, responsive website that felt modern and made its vehicle storage service easy to understand. It also needed to rank strongly in local search, bringing more relevant visits without paying for advertising.

The useful bit

I simplified the journey around the questions a potential customer needs answered, with clear service pages, focused calls to enquire and a structure built for local SEO across Nottinghamshire. The result is a site that loads quickly, works cleanly on mobile and gives searchers a straightforward route to the right information.

item.title: Riser Recliner Directory
item.description:
The brief

Riser recliner chairs are sold through several different kinds of shops, which can make it difficult for people to know where to find one in their local area. The Riser Recliner Directory needed to make that location-led purchase easier to navigate, helping people search by town or postcode, find relevant local shops and understand what each retailer can offer before making contact.

The useful bit

I designed a UK-wide directory where people can search nearby shops by location or postcode, browse retailer listings and compare detailed profiles. Each profile can show an address, phone number, website, opening hours, available services and practical features such as home demonstrations, delivery, installation, warranties, accessibility and chair customisation. Retailers can manage their own listing data, while paid boosts let shops appear at the top of listings in their county.

item.title: The Fox at Kirton
item.description:
The brief

The Fox at Kirton needed a website with enough warmth and appetite to do the pub justice, while making the practical things, including food, menus, events and bookings, easy to find.

The useful bit

I built a flexible content system with a private manager login, so the team can update menus, add events and keep opening times and other important information current without waiting for a developer. Visitors always get the latest version of the pub’s plans.

item.title: The Specialist Seating Company
item.description:
The brief

When the product range is technical and the decision is personal, a catalogue can quickly become a wall of information. The Specialist Seating Company needed a clearer way to help home carers, care homes, clinicians and hospitals find confidence.

The useful bit

I reorganised the website around needs and outcomes rather than internal product categories. Quote requests now carry the context the team needs, so the first human conversation can start with advice instead of data collection.

item.title: Tipsy Telephone
item.description:
The brief

Tipsy Telephone started with a simple idea: let wedding guests pick up a real telephone and leave a message for the couple. The challenge was to turn that charming physical experience into a reliable product that could work across many weddings without creating a large amount of manual work behind the scenes.

The brief was not just to build a booking website. It was to build the platform behind the business: the system that captures every recording, knows which wedding it belongs to, creates the couple’s private experience and delivers the finished collection after the event.
